key: Brutal Football (1994)(Millennium)[cr CSL](Disk 1 of 2).adf boot-block load +$400 to $040000 (6656 bytes):0:19CC
name: inspect_boot_block_entry
description: Thirteen-instruction routine in the boot block, reached by a PC-relative address load from one unnamed routine. The decompiler timed out, so its body is not recovered and no behaviour beyond the instruction count and caller is stated.

name: program_blitter_channels_wait
description: Loads the blitter channel pointers, modulos, masks, control words and size, waiting for the blitter to go idle before and after the writes. It calls no other routine and its purpose is not stated beyond the register writes.

name: program_blitter_sequence
description: Programs the blitter registers in a long run of channel pointers, modulos, masks and size, with busy-wait loops on the blitter status between writes. The pseudo-code shows only part of the sequence, so the full set of operations is not described.

name: program_blitter_offset_pass
description: Programs the blitter with the same register sequence as its neighbour, but takes one pointer from a shared variable plus a fixed offset. It waits for the blitter to go idle between the writes and is called by five unnamed routines.

name: update_fire_button_outputs
description: Reads two button-state bits from the CIA-A port A register and clears or sets the matching bits in an output byte reached through a stored pointer. It calls a routine before and after the update.

name: lookup_character_table_entry
description: Maps a character to an entry in one of several lookup tables: digits, uppercase and lowercase letters, and the percent, exclamation and minus symbols each have their own index, and any other character uses a default table. If the horizontal value is between 0 and 304 and a counter is positive, it calls a routine with the looked-up entry.

name: return_input_word
description: Returns its word argument unchanged and does nothing else. Two unnamed routines call it.

name: call_routine_if_in_range
description: Calls one routine, then calls a second routine only when a counter is positive and a horizontal value lies between 0 and 304. The routine is called by one unnamed routine and calls one unnamed routine.

name: call_routine_if_in_range
description: Calls one routine, then calls a second routine only when a counter is positive and a horizontal value lies between 0 and 304. The routine is called by one unnamed routine and calls one unnamed routine.

name: call_routine_if_in_range
description: Calls one routine, then calls a second routine only when a counter is positive and a horizontal value lies between 0 and 304. The routine is called by two unnamed routines and calls one unnamed routine.

name: call_routine_if_in_range
description: Calls one routine, then calls a second routine only when a counter is positive and a horizontal value lies between 0 and 304. The routine is called by four unnamed routines and calls one unnamed routine.

name: set_flag_to_minus_one
description: Stores the value minus one into a byte flag and then calls one unnamed routine. It is called by four unnamed routines.

name: stub_return_immediately
description: Contains only a return, so it does nothing when called. It is called by no recovered caller in the facts.

name: initialise_flag_sequence
description: When the flag byte is zero, runs a counted loop of seven iterations that calls a routine each time, then repeats a call-and-test loop until the flag clears, and finally sets the flag to minus one. When the flag is already non-zero it does nothing.

name: stub_empty_decompile_result
description: The decompiler produced an empty body for this routine of 73 instructions, which calls seven unnamed routines. Only the instruction count and call count are known, so no behaviour is recovered.

name: clear_text_buffer_to_spaces
description: When the flag byte is clear, writes space characters over a 27-byte buffer that starts at the flag, then sets the flag to zero.

name: poll_text_prompt_until_done
description: Resets a state byte, then repeatedly calls several unnamed routines and increments a counter until a loop condition ends. It then calls one more unnamed routine and sets the state to 20, with the referenced text Password and Select Game.

name: display_password_result_text
description: Chooses one of two paths by comparing a state byte, sets state values and calls six unnamed routines alongside the text Invalid Password, League, Round and Special. It then loops forever and never returns.

name: measure_and_trim_text
description: Measures a zero-terminated string and, on the usual path, strips trailing hyphens and spaces from a second buffer by writing zero bytes over them. When the mode argument is minus one, it instead decrements a word counter and returns the length of the string.

name: decrement_counter_and_measure
description: Decrements a word counter reached through a pointer, then returns the length of the zero-terminated string it is given.

name: measure_and_trim_text_bounded
description: Returns the length of a zero-terminated string and writes zero bytes over trailing hyphens and spaces, without moving back past a lower bound passed in a second pointer. It is the same string operation as its neighbour that also handles a sentinel mode.

name: run_option_text_sequence
description: Advances a state byte through a fixed sequence of steps, calling four unnamed routines at each step and branching on the state value. The referenced text is Knockout, League, Password and Unfriendly.

name: call_four_routines_in_order
description: Calls four unnamed routines one after another and returns, with no other work.

name: update_indexed_state_entry
description: Saves one indexed entry of a shared table, runs a fixed series of state updates with routine calls, and restores the saved entry at the end. Under one set of bit conditions it writes the value 44 into the entry before the restore.

name: read_low_bits_and_advance
description: Returns the low three bits of a shared counter and increments the counter when those bits are non-zero.

name: copy_text_replacing_spaces
description: Copies a fixed number of characters from one buffer to another, replacing each space with a hyphen, then writes a zero terminator.

name: run_startup_state_sequence
description: When the state byte is zero, calls several unnamed routines, then doubles and increments the state in a loop until it wraps to zero, runs a seven-iteration counted loop with calls, and finally sets the state to 13 and then 160.

name: read_value_until_changed
description: Reads a value through an unnamed routine repeatedly until it differs from the state byte, then stores it in the state byte and calls another unnamed routine. It runs only when the state byte is zero.

name: wait_for_value_change
description: Reads a value through an unnamed routine repeatedly until it differs from the state byte, then stores it in the state byte and calls another unnamed routine.

name: decrement_state_toward_zero
description: Decrements the state byte by one when it is non-zero and does nothing otherwise. A branch that would reset the state to zero cannot be reached as written.

name: stub_no_decompiled_body
description: The decompiler gave an empty body for a routine of 144 instructions that calls three unnamed routines, so no behaviour beyond those counts is recovered.

name: handle_text_entry_key
description: Processes a key code from the state byte for a 26-character entry buffer. It handles the backspace, delete and return codes, inserts printable characters by shifting the buffer along, and calls unnamed routines to draw or respond.

name: step_cursor_position_and_blank
description: Steps a position value forward or backward with wrap points at 10, 21 and 32, chosen by bits in a flag argument. It then writes a space into a 26-character buffer and adjusts a length counter capped at 26.

name: advance_cursor_row_wrap_blank
description: Advances a position value by one, wrapping 21 to 11 and 32 to 22. It then calls unnamed routines, writes a space into a 26-character buffer at the length position, adjusts the length counter and sets the state byte to four.

name: advance_cursor_end_wrap_blank
description: Advances a position value by one, wrapping 32 to 22 only. It then calls unnamed routines, writes a space into a 26-character buffer at the length position, adjusts the length counter and sets the state byte to four.

name: advance_cursor_and_write_blank
description: Advances a position value by one, then calls unnamed routines, writes a space into a 26-character buffer at the length position, adjusts the length counter and sets the state byte to four.

name: retreat_cursor_row_wrap_blank
description: Moves a position value back by one, wrapping 11 to 21 and 22 to 32. It then calls unnamed routines, writes a space into a 26-character buffer at the length position, adjusts the length counter and sets the state byte to four.

name: retreat_cursor_end_wrap_blank
description: Moves a position value back by one, wrapping 22 to 32 only. It then calls unnamed routines, writes a space into a 26-character buffer at the length position, adjusts the length counter and sets the state byte to four.

name: retreat_cursor_and_write_blank
description: Moves a position value back by one, then calls unnamed routines, writes a space into a 26-character buffer at the length position, adjusts the length counter and sets the state byte to four.

name: find_character_index_in_set
description: Converts a lower-case letter to upper case and returns its one-based position in a character set, or zero for a space or an absent character. The set is a fixed string of the letters A to Z, the digits one to five and the percent sign, or a buffer when the state value is above 17.

name: stub_empty_return_routine
description: Returns immediately without doing anything. The facts list a fixed character-set string as referenced text, but the body is empty.

name: find_last_non_blank_position
description: Scans a zero-terminated string and returns the one-based position of its last character that is not a space or hyphen, or zero when there is none.

name: measure_length_before_space
description: Returns the number of characters before the first space in a zero-terminated string, or zero when the string contains no space.

name: build_text_entry_table
description: Calculates a starting value from two unnamed routine results, then walks a zero-terminated string and writes each character with a position value into successive five-word records of a table. The position advances by three for each character, and the routine loops until the state byte changes.

name: update_table_record_positions
description: Walks a table of five-word records, subtracting each velocity word from its position word and clamping the position against a limit word. It sets the state byte to 255 in one branch and calls an unnamed routine when the position lies inside fixed bounds.

name: initialise_record_table_positions
description: Fills a fixed number of five-word records with values: a position computed from the state byte, a velocity of plus or minus five depending on the sign of an intermediate value, and a fixed value of ten in one field. The state byte advances by two for each record.

name: advance_records_and_test_range
description: Runs 255 times over a table of five-word records, adding each velocity word to its position word. It clears the state byte when any position lies strictly between minus 40 and 330.

name: advance_records_call_in_range
description: Sets the state byte to one, then runs 255 times over a table of five-word records, adding each velocity word to its position word. When a position lies strictly between minus 40 and 360, it clears the state byte and calls an unnamed routine.

name: measure_text_line_width
description: Subtracts a value returned by an unnamed routine from a width counter, then scans a zero-terminated string. A period adds one, a newline resets the counter to zero, and any other character calls an unnamed routine and adds three.

name: accumulate_text_line_width
description: Scans a zero-terminated string and accumulates a width counter. A period adds one, a newline resets the counter to zero, and any other character calls an unnamed routine and adds three.

name: scan_text_newlines_and_call
description: Walks a zero-terminated string, resetting the counter to zero at each newline and adding one to it. For every other character it calls an unnamed routine and adds two.

name: advance_counter_per_text_line
description: Repeatedly calls an unnamed routine and adds two to a counter, skipping newlines in a zero-terminated string by resetting the counter at each one. It returns when it reaches the end of the string.

name: stub_empty_return_routine
description: Returns immediately without doing anything. The routine has no other instructions.

name: call_routine_for_letter
description: Calls one unnamed routine only when the character argument is an upper-case or lower-case letter. Other characters return unchanged.

name: halt_in_infinite_loop
description: Loops forever without doing anything, so control never returns. The decompiler shows an empty infinite loop.

name: save_and_repoint_global
description: Stores the current value of a global into a saved slot, sets a pointer variable to the address of the global, and then sets a second value to a fixed address. It then returns.

name: update_joystick_button_flags
description: Updates two button-flag bits in a structure, clearing or keeping each depending on a mode value and on the CIA-A port A register bits. It calls an unnamed routine before each update.

name: poll_joystick_and_mouse_ports
description: Touches the joystick and mouse port data registers, the fire-button register and the interrupt enable register, as listed in the hardware references. The attached pseudo-code shows a different routine, so the description is taken from the register list only.

name: apply_clamped_record_motion
description: When the mode byte is not two, calls an unnamed routine and, for mode one, clears a flag bit. When it is two, stores a new position, moves two coordinates by the change, and clamps them between bounds held in the record, with the direction set by a flag byte.

name: build_five_bit_status_mask
description: Looks up five bytes of a record in a shared table and clears one bit of a mask for each lookup that is non-zero. It stores the resulting mask at offset six of the record.

name: apply_table_motion_and_clamp
description: Looks up a motion entry in a table using a small index formed from bits of an argument, and stores the entry's flag byte at offset six of a record. It adds the entry's two deltas to the record's coordinates and clamps the coordinates between bounds held in the record.

name: program_blitter_draw_sequence
description: Writes a series of blitter setups with channel pointers, modulos, masks and a shift value derived from the arguments, waiting for the blitter to go idle between passes and then loading a prepared register set. The decompiled output was truncated, so only the early part of the routine is described.

name: fill_and_load_blitter_record
description: Fills a record of blitter pointers, modulos, masks and a size value from the arguments and a global value. It then waits for the blitter to go idle and loads the record into the blitter registers, selecting one of two source records.

name: load_blitter_record_from_arguments
description: Fills a blitter record from two arguments and a global value, then loads the record into the blitter registers from one of two source records. The routine waits for the blitter to go idle before and after the loads.

name: build_blitter_span_record
description: Fills a blitter record from a global value and an argument, using a fixed pointer constant and a fixed control word, then loads it into the blitter registers from one of two sources. The facts list four unnamed calls that do not appear in the shown pseudo-code.

name: stub_empty_return_routine
description: Returns immediately without doing anything. It is referenced by one unnamed routine.

name: load_blitter_record_from_offset
description: Stores a masked control word and two pointer values into a blitter record derived from an argument, then stores a position value. It loads the record into the blitter registers from one of two source records, waiting for the blitter to go idle before and after.

name: load_blitter_record_pair_fixed
description: Writes a control word and a fixed pointer constant into a blitter record at two offsets in turn, waiting for the blitter to go idle after each write. It then loads the record into the blitter registers from one of two source records.

name: setup_copper_list_and_interrupts
description: Runs a state byte through counter and selection steps, then clears it while calling several unnamed routines. The facts list copper list location and jump registers, interrupt request registers and the potential-I/O control register, none of which the shown pseudo-code writes.

name: advance_four_channel_state
description: When the state byte is zero, calls an unnamed routine and derives a value from the low two bits of a word, toggling a direction byte when those bits are zero. It then copies four stored values in turn into a slot indexed zero to three and calls an unnamed routine after each copy.

name: toggle_and_clear_four_bytes
description: Toggles a flag byte, and when the result is non-zero, checks four consecutive bytes and calls an unnamed routine for each non-zero one. It then clears those four bytes to zero.

name: initialise_audio_channel_state
description: Stores the tag MODS in a structure and walks six relative offsets to fill a table of pointers, then sets initial state bytes to 64. It stores the hardware address of each of four audio channels in its record, sets volume and channel fields, and writes the DMA control register to clear the four audio channel bits.

name: clear_word_buffer
description: Writes zero to 88 consecutive words, starting at the pointer argument.

name: configure_channel_record_if_enabled
description: When a flag bit is set, sets one bit of a mask for the channel number argument. It then writes a pointer computed from a table and fixed offsets into a per-channel record, and sets three byte fields of that record.

name: clear_flags_then_update_channels
description: Clears two status bytes in a record. If a pointer field is non-zero and a flag in the second structure is set, it calls several unnamed routines and returns; otherwise, if another flag is set, it calls five unnamed routines.

name: update_record_when_flag_set
description: Reads a flag byte at offset 57 of a structure and clears its lowest bit. If the bit was set, it writes a word into the record that the structure's first field points to, computed from a word at offset 22 doubled plus a longword at offset 4, then copies a word from offset 24 after it.

name: check_flag_and_set_status
description: Reads a flag byte at offset 56 of a structure and clears its lowest bit. When the bit was set, it sets a byte at offset 57 to minus one and writes a word into another structure at offset 150, using a word from offset 46 combined with a fixed bit pattern.

name: interpret_sequence_commands
description: Runs a timed command interpreter over a byte stream held in a structure, reading opcodes and dispatching them through a jump table that sets fields, sets pointers, calls unnamed routines or stops. The decompiler reports bad instruction data in part of the table, so the full set of opcodes is not recovered.

name: dispatch_sequence_command_entry
description: Enters the same command interpreter at a later point, reading one opcode from the stream and dispatching it. The decompiler reports the same bad instruction data as its neighbour, so only the shared dispatch structure is described.

name: run_sequence_countdown_block
description: Enters the same command dispatch code, calls an unnamed routine and stores the stream pointer into the structure, then loops over a countdown that reads a per-channel counter. The decompiled output was cut off and reports bad instruction data.

name: resume_sequence_command_dispatch
description: Enters the same command interpreter at a later point and dispatches the next opcode. The decompiler reports bad instruction data and the output was cut off, so the full set of opcodes is not recovered.

name: store_sequence_byte_in_field
description: Enters the same command interpreter at a point that stores one stream byte into a structure field and then continues dispatch. The decompiler reports bad instruction data and the output was cut off.

name: test_sequence_byte_then_dispatch
description: Enters the same command interpreter at a point that tests the next stream byte for zero and calls an unnamed routine only when it is non-zero. It then continues dispatch, and the decompiler reports bad instruction data.

name: store_sequence_byte_word_field
description: Enters the same command interpreter at a point that reads one stream byte into the data register and stores it in a word field of the structure. It then advances the stream and continues dispatch.

name: store_sequence_byte_and_advance
description: Enters the same command interpreter at a point that reads one stream byte, stores it in a word field of the structure and advances the stream. It then continues dispatch.

name: call_three_routines_in_order
description: Calls three unnamed routines one after another and returns, with no other work.

name: scale_and_clamp_value
description: Multiplies two words of a structure and shifts the product right by six, scales the result by a word from another structure and shifts right again, then stores it. The stored value is clamped so that anything above 64 becomes 64, except 65, which becomes zero, and the result is written to offset eight of a second structure.

name: advance_indexed_table_step
description: When a pointer field is non-zero, adds a signed byte from a table, scaled by a shift, to a word at offset 50 of the structure. It then advances an index and wraps it to twice a stored value when the index reaches a limit.

name: update_timed_level_envelope
description: When the active flag byte is set, computes a level from a base byte, a slope and a divisor, then decrements a step counter. When the counter reaches minus one it either clears the flag or calls a routine selected from a table by the flag byte, and the level is stored as a word at offset 50.

name: clear_active_flag_byte
description: Writes zero to the active flag byte at offset 58 of a structure and returns.

name: load_envelope_from_table_entry
description: When a table pointer field is non-zero, copies values from offsets one, three and four of the table entry into envelope fields and sets the state byte to two.

name: reset_level_word_to_64
description: Writes the value 64 into the word at offset 50 of a structure and returns.

name: negate_envelope_slope_and_restart
description: When a table pointer field is non-zero, clears one envelope byte and stores the negated value of another byte as a step. It loads a count from offset five of the table entry into two counter bytes and sets the state byte to minus one.

name: update_position_and_counter
description: Updates a scaled offset from a table indexed by a counter, with the index wrapping to twice a stored value at its limit. If a counter byte is set, it adds a step value to an accumulator and decrements the counter, then writes the sum of the offset and the accumulator into a field of the record its first pointer names.

name: start_channel_from_table_entry
description: When a table entry pointer is non-zero, copies a start value and table bytes into envelope fields and sets a state byte to four. It writes a word from another field to the register at offset 150 from a base register, sets up a list entry with a zero word and a reset value, and sets a status byte to minus one.

name: select_record_when_index_changes
description: When an index byte differs from the stored value, stores the new index and looks up a 32-byte record in a table by that index. It then copies the record's fields into the structure's counter, step and pointer fields.

name: clear_flag_and_update_ptr
description: Clears the lowest bit of a flag byte at offset 145 of a structure. If the bit was set, it writes a word into the record its first field points to, computed from a word at offset 110 doubled plus a longword at offset 92, and writes a word copied from offset 112 into the record four bytes after the first word.

name: inspect_undecompiled_routine
description: A two-instruction routine whose decompilation timed out, so no body is recovered. It is called by one unnamed routine.

name: copy_boot_code_low_memory
description: Boot-block entry that copies three blocks of code into low memory with counted loops and sets a few values in a structure. It calls three unnamed routines, jumps to a routine copied to a computed address, and loops forever if a library result is zero.

name: toggle_bit_at_offset
description: Stores the value 512 into a global, then toggles one bit, selected by an argument, in a byte at an address computed from a base and the argument. It then calls one unnamed routine.

name: hash_string_and_find_entry
description: Computes a rotating checksum and a running sum over a zero-terminated string, then walks a linked list for an entry whose second field equals the argument string. If none matches and the size argument is above 40, it appends a new entry after the last one and calls unnamed routines.

name: allocate_and_copy_loader_block
description: Allocates memory through the Exec library and fills in an I/O request, using the AllocMem and DoIO library calls listed in its facts. It then copies 1375 longwords from a code routine into the allocated memory and jumps to it, and it loops forever if the allocation fails.

name: copy_boot_blocks_toggle_bit
description: Copies 256 longwords of boot-block data into a fixed low-memory area, then copies 8192 bytes into a second area, and toggles one bit in a byte at a computed address. The facts also list a background colour register write and the text CODE, which the pseudo-code does not show.

name: clear_and_fill_memory_blocks
description: Zeroes 2000 longwords at one fixed address, copies 25 longwords at a spacing of ten longwords into a second area and 25 words into a third, then writes a terminator value and sets the global to a fixed address. The facts list copper list location and jump registers, which the pseudo-code does not write.

name: wait_for_raster_position
description: Busy-waits on the vertical and horizontal position register value until it is no longer below minus 1535, then returns.

name: copy_vector_block_and_load
description: Copies 29 longwords from a routine into a low-memory vector area, makes a system trap call and calls a library routine. If the library result is non-zero it copies 1375 longwords to a computed address and jumps there; otherwise it loops forever.

name: copy_vector_block_and_load
description: Copies 29 longwords from a routine into a low-memory vector area, makes a system trap call and calls a library routine. If the library result is non-zero it copies 1375 longwords to a computed address and jumps there; otherwise it loops forever.

name: copy_second_block_and_load
description: Copies 29 longwords from a routine into a second low-memory area, makes a system trap call and calls a library routine. If the library result is non-zero it copies 1375 longwords to a computed address and jumps there; otherwise it loops forever.

name: write_jump_opcode_toggle_bit
description: Writes a fixed 32-bit value that encodes a 68000 absolute jump instruction to a fixed address. It then toggles one bit, selected by an argument, in a byte at a computed address and calls one unnamed routine.

name: copy_second_block_and_load
description: Copies 29 longwords from a routine into a second low-memory area, makes a system trap call and calls a library routine. If the library result is non-zero it copies 1375 longwords to a computed address and jumps there; otherwise it loops forever.

name: run_boot_block_loader
description: Boot-block entry that makes system trap calls and a library call, and sets a fixed value in memory. It copies 256 longwords to low memory and 8192 bytes into a second area, toggles one bit in a byte at a computed address, and calls one unnamed routine.

name: run_boot_loader_with_doio
description: Sets up an I/O request through the Exec library's DoIO call with fixed size and status fields. It then copies 256 longwords to low memory and 8192 bytes into a second area, and toggles one bit in a byte at a computed address after calling three unnamed routines.

name: copy_code_and_toggle_bit
description: Copies 256 longwords of code to a fixed low-memory area, makes a system trap call, and copies 8192 bytes into a second area. It toggles one bit in a byte at a computed address after calling one unnamed routine.

name: copy_bytes_and_toggle_bit
description: Copies 8192 bytes from the boot block into a second area, calls one unnamed routine, and toggles one bit in a byte at a computed address. The facts list a background colour register write and the text CODE, which the pseudo-code does not show.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The decompiler produced only a bad-instruction marker for this routine of 138 instructions, which one unnamed routine calls. No behaviour is recovered from the body.

name: run_boot_block_loader
description: Boot-block entry that makes system trap calls and a library call, and sets a fixed value in memory. It copies 256 longwords to low memory and 8192 bytes into a second area, toggles one bit in a byte at a computed address, and calls one unnamed routine.

name: decompress_boot_image_stream
description: Decompresses a bit-packed stream into memory by choosing literal, back-reference or run-length paths from bits read off the stream, with a marker byte introducing a run of one repeated byte. Each output word is written to the colour register, which the facts list as COLOR16.

key: Robocop 3 (1991)(Ocean)(M3)[cr FLT](Disk 1 of 3).adf boot-block load +$D6800 to $060000 (20480 bytes):0:0116
name: refill_bit_buffer_word
description: Reads a longword just before the current input pointer and writes its low byte to a destination byte. It returns the longword shifted right by one with the top bit set as a refill marker.

key: Robocop 3 (1991)(Ocean)(M3)[cr FLT](Disk 1 of 3).adf boot-block load +$D6800 to $060000 (20480 bytes):0:0130
name: skip_bits_with_refill
description: Shifts a bit register right by the number of places given by a count argument, calling an unnamed routine to refill the register whenever it becomes zero.

key: Robocop 3 (1991)(Ocean)(M3)[cr FLT](Disk 2 of 3).adf boot-block load +$3800 to $020000 (8192 bytes):0:0004
